planning_notes: Preserve all supplied connections. As explicitly resolved, resistor1 through resistor4 are 10 kOhm external pull-downs despite the embedded component value fields; all button inputs use INPUT without internal pull-ups.
The environment guarantees at most one button is held at a time, permitting four mutually exclusive physical buzzer outputs on the single native tone channel.

The SysML model commands 262 Hz for Do, 294 Hz for Re, 330 Hz for Mi, and 349 Hz for Fa while the corresponding button is pressed, and commands zero on all other buzzers. With no button pressed, every buzzer is silent.
All buzzers start silent. Evaluate button-to-tone behavior every 5 ms, within the 250 ms reaction bound; setup must return within 500 ms.
Tone uses Timer2, which conflicts with Uno PWM on D3 and D11. This circuit uses D3 as a digital input and D11 as a tone output, not PWM, so no PWM resource conflict is introduced.
No serial reporting or business-time input is required.

# Piano Keyboard

## Project Description
This is an Arduino project that creates a piano keyboard using four push buttons and four buzzers corresponding to the notes Do, Re, Mi, and Fa.

## Hardware Components
- Arduino Uno
- Push Button * 4
- 10kΩ resistor * 4
- Piezoelectric Buzzer * 4

## Circuit Description
Four piezo buzzers and four push buttons are connected to an Arduino Uno. Button 1 and Buzzer 1 correspond to the note Do, Button 2 and Buzzer 2 to Re, Button 3 and Buzzer 3 to Mi, and Button 4 and Buzzer 4 to Fa. Buttons 1 through 4 are connected to Arduino pins 2, 3, 4, and 5, respectively. When the button is not pressed, the input pin is connected to gnd3 through a 10kΩ resistor. When the button is pressed, the input pin is connected to 5v. 
The positive pins of the buzzers are connected to Arduino pins 9, 10, 11, and 12, respectively, and their negative pins are connected to gnd3.

## Expected Behavior
When the Arduino powers up, it should:
1. Configure button pins as INPUT
2. Configure buzzer pins as OUTPUT
3. Continuously monitor the button state, and if it reads HIGH, play a tone on the corresponding buzzer
4. If no button is pressed, keep all buzzers silent

## Success Criteria
The test is successful when:
1. The buzzer plays a tone when the corresponding button is pressed.

## Notes for Implementation
- The button input will read HIGH when it is pressed.
- When the button is not pressed, pin1.l is connected to pin1.r and pin2.l is connected to pin2.r. When the button is pressed, all the pins are connected together.
- The frequencies of Do, Re, Mi, and Fa are 262 Hz, 294 Hz, 330 Hz, and 349 Hz, respectively.
- Only one button is pressed at a time.

## Attributes
- To use 10kΩ resistor, set the property name "value" to "10000 ohm".

Operational acceptance profile operational-acceptance-v4 (additional public experimental conditions, not raw dataset text):
- Explicit original requirements and supplied circuit connections override every default below.
- Where no electrical wiring is supplied, individual LEDs are active HIGH to GND and buttons connect the named input to GND with INPUT_PULLUP; model pressed values are normalized independently of electrical level.
- When unspecified, a counter starts at zero and an LED starts OFF. An explicitly required ON state takes precedence.
- When the original gives no reaction deadline, a digital/button/serial command, PWM duty command or servo ANGLE COMMAND must update within 250ms of its input event becoming available. This does not impose physical motor travel time, shorten an explicit delay, or change a specified sensor/report period.
- When the original gives no display refresh period or response deadline, a changed input must be reflected in the display within 250ms. Explicit original display periods, delays and startup sequences override this default. This additional display bound was explicitly authorized for this experimental variant.
- Where the requirement asks to continuously stream a Boolean button/switch state over Serial but gives no repeat interval, respond to a changed state within 250ms and emit its correct state message at least once in every 500ms stable-state interval after settling. Explicit original report periods and event-only reporting rules override this default. This authorized additional continuous-state-report condition does not apply to startup-only messages, command echoes, sensor sampling or persistent display contents. A display retaining the correct visible state requires no repeated print calls unless the source explicitly requires redraws.
- Unless the original specifies a warmup or delayed startup, setup() must return within 500ms. Deadlines stated after initialization are measured from the observed setup() return, not power-on.
- An unspecified continuous DHT report must eventually emit a fresh valid reading within 3000ms of that measurement becoming available; explicit reporting periods override this bound.

# Piano Keyboard

## Project Description
This is an Arduino project that creates a piano keyboard using four push buttons and four buzzers corresponding to the notes Do, Re, Mi, and Fa.

## Hardware Components
- Arduino Uno
- Push Button * 4
- 10kΩ resistor * 4
- Piezoelectric Buzzer * 4

## Circuit Description
Four piezo buzzers and four push buttons are connected to an Arduino Uno. Button 1 and Buzzer 1 correspond to the note Do, Button 2 and Buzzer 2 to Re, Button 3 and Buzzer 3 to Mi, and Button 4 and Buzzer 4 to Fa. Buttons 1 through 4 are connected to Arduino pins 2, 3, 4, and 5, respectively. When the button is not pressed, the input pin is connected to gnd3 through a 10kΩ resistor. When the button is pressed, the input pin is connected to 5v. 
The positive pins of the buzzers are connected to Arduino pins 9, 10, 11, and 12, respectively, and their negative pins are connected to gnd3.

## Expected Behavior
When the Arduino powers up, it should:
1. Configure button pins as INPUT
2. Configure buzzer pins as OUTPUT
3. Continuously monitor the button state, and if it reads HIGH, play a tone on the corresponding buzzer
4. If no button is pressed, keep all buzzers silent

## Success Criteria
The test is successful when:
1. The buzzer plays a tone when the corresponding button is pressed.

## Notes for Implementation
- The button input will read HIGH when it is pressed.
- When the button is not pressed, pin1.l is connected to pin1.r and pin2.l is connected to pin2.r. When the button is pressed, all the pins are connected together.
- The frequencies of Do, Re, Mi, and Fa are 262 Hz, 294 Hz, 330 Hz, and 349 Hz, respectively.
- Only one button is pressed at a time.

## Attributes
- To use 10kΩ resistor, set the property name "value" to "10000 ohm".

Disclosed resolution of the source component-value inconsistency: the explicit prose and Attributes instruction specifying10kOhm button pull-down resistors take precedence over the contradictory resistor value fields in the embedded circuit. Preserve every connection and MCU pin. This bench variant uses10kOhm external pull-downs, buttons active HIGH and INPUT without internal pull-ups; only one button is held at a time.
Operational acceptance profile operational-acceptance-v4 (additional public experimental conditions, not raw dataset text):
- Explicit original requirements and supplied circuit connections override every default below.
- Where no electrical wiring is supplied, individual LEDs are active HIGH to GND and buttons connect the named input to GND with INPUT_PULLUP; model pressed values are normalized independently of electrical level.
- When unspecified, a counter starts at zero and an LED starts OFF. An explicitly required ON state takes precedence.
- When the original gives no reaction deadline, a digital/button/serial command, PWM duty command or servo ANGLE COMMAND must update within 250ms of its input event becoming available. This does not impose physical motor travel time, shorten an explicit delay, or change a specified sensor/report period.
- When the original gives no display refresh period or response deadline, a changed input must be reflected in the display within 250ms. Explicit original display periods, delays and startup sequences override this default. This additional display bound was explicitly authorized for this experimental variant.
- Where the requirement asks to continuously stream a Boolean button/switch state over Serial but gives no repeat interval, respond to a changed state within 250ms and emit its correct state message at least once in every 500ms stable-state interval after settling. Explicit original report periods and event-only reporting rules override this default. This authorized additional continuous-state-report condition does not apply to startup-only messages, command echoes, sensor sampling or persistent display contents. A display retaining the correct visible state requires no repeated print calls unless the source explicitly requires redraws.
- Unless the original specifies a warmup or delayed startup, setup() must return within 500ms. Deadlines stated after initialization are measured from the observed setup() return, not power-on.
- An unspecified continuous DHT report must eventually emit a fresh valid reading within 3000ms of that measurement becoming available; explicit reporting periods override this bound.

requirement_checks.requirement_quote: Continuously monitor the button state, and if it reads HIGH, play a tone on the corresponding buzzer
requirement_checks.reason: The four current input levels select the required Do, Re, Mi and Fa frequencies, respectively, with zero selecting silence. Contract bindings preserve buttons on D2–D5 and corresponding buzzers on D9–D12, use active-HIGH inputs without pull-ups, and interpret output commands in Hz. Registered acquisition samples before the first tick, so an initially held button sounds without needing an edge; holds sustain the command and releases clear it. All-false inputs and initial output commands are silent. There is no persistent state or update-order hazard. The single-button assumption is compatible with exclusive tone outputs. The explicit 10 kOhm resolution overrides the stale embedded resistor values while preserving wiring. Input, controller and output periods of 5 ms are consistent with the additional 250 ms response bound. No modeled startup delay contradicts the 500 ms setup bound. Display, serial, DHT, LED and counter defaults are inapplicable. These findings establish model-boundary consistency, not execution success.

requirement_checks.requirement_quote: The frequencies of Do, Re, Mi, and Fa are 262 Hz, 294 Hz, 330 Hz, and 349 Hz, respectively.
requirement_checks.reason: Each button controls its corresponding buzzer at exactly the specified frequency, with no scaling. False inputs command zero, defined by the contract as silence, including at startup with no button pressed and after release. Direct level dependence handles startup presses and sustained holds without edge-history or retained-state defects. The contract specifies the supplied Uno, all four input and output devices, the required D2–D5 and D9–D12 mappings, and active-HIGH digital inputs with pullup=false. Normative acquisition facts specify INPUT configuration; tone-output bindings are consistent with buzzer OUTPUT configuration. Supply and ground wiring is preserved. The disclosed component-value resolution makes 10 kOhm external pull-downs authoritative over the contradictory embedded values. At most one nonzero command occurs within the stipulated one-button-at-a-time operating boundary, consistent with exclusive tone channels. Actual initialization and peripheral execution remain downstream obligations.

limitations: This is a model-boundary review, not final code acceptance. Supplied test descriptions are not executed evidence.

Verify that generated or assembled hardware applies the explicitly authoritative 10 kOhm pull-down resolution while preserving every connection; embedded resistor value fields still contain the overridden values.
